tasks.short: Tell applicants the approved hiring outcome and record the communication.

steps.what: Find the approved hiring decision and check candidate contact details.
Prepare an acceptance or rejection message from the approved template.
Check the recipient, outcome, terms and wording before release.
Call applicants when the outcome needs a personal explanation.
Send the approved written outcome to the applicant.
Record the communication and create any follow-up reminder.

tasks.design: Configure the {ATS} to assemble messages from approved decisions, terms and templates, then queue them for recruiter release. Bind approval to the exact message and recipient; stop release if either changes or the decision is withdrawn. Log delivery and follow-up automatically, while recruiters handle personal conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions, offer terms and message templates were maintained separately. Staff copied information between records and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template and approval features may cover most work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting missing fields and delivery events.
tasks.still_hard: Late decision changes, contested rejection reasons and negotiated offers need careful handling. Reliable delivery status may require an additional connection.
tasks.human_edge: Explain disappointing news with care, answer questions and recognise when an applicant needs a conversation.

ambition.what: Offer a scheduled outcome conversation to interviewed applicants who request one.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time copying messages and more time resolving missed communications and arranging candidate conversations. Hiring decision rights remain with the hiring team.

reach.learn: Distinguish approved, job-related feedback from speculative or inappropriate explanations.

evidence.claim: Template messages, approval queues and communication logging can usually be configured in recruitment systems.
AFAS documents HR workflow capabilities and applicant matching with the recruiter deciding; this supports workflow feasibility, not this exact notification design.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated significant decisions; sending a previously approved outcome is distinct from deciding that outcome.

assumptions: Step shares are planning estimates for a mixed caseload, not measured company time.
The hiring decision already exists before this task starts.
Personal calls occur for a subset of applicants; their share is averaged across the caseload.
Approved templates make a model loop unnecessary for routine messages.
Build ranges describe a small initial rollout and may overlap.
unknowns: Whether the {ATS} supports approval-bound sending, delivery events and cancellation.
Who can approve rejection wording and offer terms.
Which applicants normally receive calls.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed workflow.
research_questions: Can configuration prevent duplicate sends and invalidate approval after any relevant change?
Which notification failures currently cause the most candidate follow-up?
new_work: Review queued messages and handle delivery failures.
Maintain approved templates and access permissions.
Check that withdrawn decisions cancel pending messages.
Maintain any connection between the {ATS} and {EMAIL}.

tasks.short: Check applicants against job requirements and refer suitable applicants to the hiring team.

steps.what: Open applications and confirm the current screening requirements.
Read application documents and note evidence against each requirement.

loop.input: Application documents and versioned, job-related screening criteria.
loop.output: Requirement-by-requirement evidence with source passages and explicit missing information; no applicant ranking.
loop.check: Validate the output schema and source passages. The reviewer checks consequential evidence and all unclear findings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per application; unreadable or unsupported evidence goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields do not capture all relevant evidence in varied application documents.

steps.what: Ask applicants to clarify missing or ambiguous required information.
Decide which applicants meet the requirements and document the reasoning.
Refer selected applicants with supporting evidence to the hiring team.

tasks.design: Use the {ATS} for worklists, fixed completeness checks, clarification templates and referrals. A bounded extraction loop on the {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts evidence with source passages; the assistant makes the screening decision before the {ATS} releases a referral. Assess the intended use under GDPR and the EU AI Act before rollout, with national rules considered separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Application documents vary, and equivalent experience rarely maps cleanly to fixed fields. Fully automatic ranking risks hiding unsupported assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can organise document evidence for review. Deterministic checks and existing {ATS} workflows handle completeness and routing.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing equivalent experience, accommodations and ambiguous requirements remains difficult. Human review must be substantive, and recruitment AI classification depends on actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise transferable experience, challenge unnecessary requirements and explain a screening decision fairly.

ambition.what: Provide a transferable-experience review route for applicants changing careers.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time assessing uncertain evidence and discussing transferable experience with specialists. They gain a defined escalation route for equivalence questions; final hiring authority stays with the hiring team.

reach.task: Review whether screening requirements reflect essential job needs.
reach.learn: Job analysis, evidence-based selection and assessment of equivalent experience.

reach.task: Review patterns in disputed screening decisions.
reach.learn: Appropriate aggregate comparisons, privacy limits and investigation of possible barriers.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents applicant matching with the recruiter deciding.
Recruitment and selection uses are listed within the EU AI Act high-risk categories.
The EU AI Act classification rules distinguish some narrow procedural uses; a preparation label alone does not settle classification.
Source-linked extraction can support review, but its accuracy and time savings require local validation.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are estimates to validate during a pilot.
The assistant screens under agreed criteria and escalates ambiguous equivalence questions.
The model extracts evidence without scoring, ranking or automatically rejecting applicants.
Missing evidence is recorded as unknown rather than treated as failure.
Consent and access ranges include privacy review, classification assessment and applicable employee consultation; formal obligations may extend delivery.
unknowns: Whether the assistant currently has authority to make initial screening decisions.
Which criteria are essential, negotiable or legally restricted.
Whether the {ATS} already provides suitable evidence extraction.
Application languages, document quality and availability of structured fields.
Applicable national consultation requirements and the intended system's legal classification.
research_questions: Does extraction preserve qualifications and equivalent experience across the application languages used?
Which ambiguous criteria generate the most inconsistent human decisions?
Can reviewers inspect original documents without being anchored by a generated summary?
new_work: Verify extracted evidence and resolve unsupported passages.
Maintain versioned screening criteria and clarification templates.
Sample decisions for missed evidence and inconsistent treatment.
Monitor extraction quality after document or model changes.
Maintain access controls, retention settings and the intended-use assessment.

tasks.short: Prepare vacancy postings, arrange publication and notify eligible employees.

steps.what: Collect the approved vacancy details and recruitment timetable.
Adapt approved vacancy wording to internal and external posting formats.
Approve posting content, channels, audience and advertising spend.
Publish the vacancy internally and on approved external channels.
Identify eligible employees and send the approved vacancy notice.
Check live postings and track corrections, closing dates and removal.

tasks.design: Generate channel-specific postings from approved vacancy fields in the {ATS}, using fixed templates and validation rules. Configure publication through existing connections to the {CMS} and {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and use explicit {HCM} rules for internal notices. A scheduled check on the {DATA_PLATFORM} flags failed publication, mismatched fields and overdue removal for human follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channels required separate forms, and internal notices depended on manually maintained recipient lists. Approval and publication status were scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing publication connections and reusable field mappings can remove repeated entry. AI-assisted coding makes small format adapters and status checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Some channels lack reliable interfaces or return incomplete status information. Eligibility rules, wording and advertising choices still need human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose appropriate channels and challenge vacancy wording or eligibility restrictions that unnecessarily exclude people.

ambition.what: Provide timely internal vacancy notices to employees on leave who opt into them.

tasks.altitude: The assistant manages publication exceptions and helps recruiters compare channel performance. They can coordinate corrections within the approved plan; advertising budget decisions remain with the budget holder.

reach.task: Review recruitment-channel results for a vacancy family.
reach.learn: Compare qualified applications and recruitment cost without confusing volume with suitability.

evidence.claim: Structured templates and existing recruitment-system publication connections can reduce repeated vacancy entry.
AFAS documents HR self-service and recruitment capabilities, supporting the feasibility of connected HR workflows.
Fixed channel formatting and explicit employee-audience rules do not require a model.

assumptions: Step shares are estimates for a typical vacancy, not measured company time.
Vacancy wording has already been approved; this task adapts formats rather than inventing the role.
The initial rollout uses channels with existing publication connections.
Internal notices use explicit eligibility rules rather than inferred employee suitability.
Build ranges include access setup and applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: Which channels have supported connections and publication status events.
Whether employee records support accurate internal audience rules.
Who approves spend and publication changes.
Whether employees on leave can receive optional vacancy notices through approved contact channels.
Applicable national requirements for internal vacancy access and consultation.
research_questions: Which repeated channel fields can be mapped without losing required wording?
Can closing and removal status be checked reliably on each initial channel?
Which employee groups currently miss internal vacancy notices?
new_work: Maintain channel mappings and vacancy templates.
Handle publication failures and posting discrepancies.
Check eligibility rules when employment policies change.
Approve corrections and verify expired postings are removed.

tasks.short: Obtain authorised applicant references and background-check information for a human hiring assessment.

steps.what: Confirm which reference and background checks are necessary and legally permitted.
Obtain required applicant notices, referee details and any necessary authorisation.
Send approved reference requests or submit an authorised official-check request.
Discuss job-related reference questions with the referee by telephone.
Chase outstanding replies and record unavailable or declined checks.
Check response identity, completeness and discrepancies; assemble the restricted check file.
Assess discrepancies and refer relevant findings to the authorised hiring decision-maker.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted check register in the {ATS} or {WORKFLOW}, with approved scope, notices, request templates, deadlines and retention controls. Send only authorised requests and bounded reminders through {EMAIL}; store necessary evidence with restricted access in {DOCS}. Remove unnecessary checks at scope review, while people conduct reference conversations, verify discrepancies and assess findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: External replies arrive through varied channels, and permissible checks differ by role and national rules. Sensitive information was often tracked through individual mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, request templates, reminder rules and restricted records already cover much of the coordination. Small connections can bring status into one register without automating the hiring assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Referee identity, incomplete responses and disputed statements require investigation. Criminal-record information has specific GDPR restrictions, and candidate permission alone does not establish that a check is lawful.
tasks.human_edge: Ask proportionate questions, distinguish facts from opinion and give applicants a fair chance to address discrepancies.

ambition.what: Provide a documented applicant discrepancy-resolution process before adverse findings reach a hiring decision.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing replies and more time resolving evidence gaps with applicants and referees. They coordinate the discrepancy process; the specialist and hiring manager retain assessment and hiring authority.

reach.learn: Evidence provenance, proportionate checks, applicant correction rights and escalation under national rules.

evidence.claim: Request templates, bounded reminders and restricted check registers can use existing workflow features.
GDPR Article 10 specifically restricts processing of criminal-conviction and offence data; national authorisation requirements vary.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Human conversations and assessments can remain manual while their preparation and coordination are automated.

assumptions: Step shares average a mixed caseload; official checks and telephone references do not occur in every case.
Routine European practice centres on proportionate references and permitted checks, rather than unrestricted enquiries to law enforcement.
The baseline uses written requests; mandatory portal or paper routes require separate local steps and effort estimates.
Unnecessary checks are omitted at scope review rather than created as a separate recurring step.
Reminders repeat an already approved request, disclose no additional information, have a fixed limit and stop on reply or withdrawal.
No model processes reference or criminal-record content in this design.
Build ranges include privacy review, restricted access and applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: Which checks are legally required or permitted for the roles and countries involved.
Whether official information must be supplied by the applicant or obtained through an authorised route.
Which requests require a portal, paper form or verified identity.
Who can access findings and how long each evidence category must be retained.
Whether the {ATS} can restrict sensitive check evidence separately from ordinary candidate records.
Who has authority to resolve disputed findings and pause a hiring decision.
research_questions: Which existing checks lack a documented necessity or permitted basis?
Which response channels create the most chasing and identity-verification work?
Can the register retain a necessary check outcome without retaining excessive underlying information?
new_work: Maintain permitted-check policies by role and applicable national rules.
Handle failed requests, unavailable referees and portal exceptions.
Review discrepancies with applicants and specialists.
Audit access and enforce evidence-retention rules.
Maintain reminder limits and stop conditions.

role.altitude: The role shifts from repeated entry, publication and chasing toward candidate communication, evidence verification and exception coordination. Hiring, screening-policy and sensitive-check decisions remain with explicitly authorised people.
reach: Human Resources Specialists: review transferable experience and disputed check evidence.
Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers: investigate recurring barriers in screening.
Human Resources Managers: assess candidate communication and recruitment-process exceptions.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, templates, approval rules and bounded reminders.
Read integration logs and resolve failed handoffs.
Verify source evidence and recognise unsupported model extraction.
Conduct fair candidate and referee conversations.
Apply GDPR, recruitment AI requirements and relevant national rules.
Analyse process outcomes without turning administrative indicators into hiring scores.
role.ambitious_version: Become a recruitment operations coordinator who runs a candidate discrepancy-resolution service, improves internal vacancy access and brings evidence about recurring process failures to HR specialists.

job.title: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
